tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Hanoi move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a clean stack of n disks from a source peg to a target peg using an auxiliary peg, first recursively move the top n‑1 disks to the auxiliary, then move the largest disk to the target, then recursively move the n‑1 disks from the auxiliary onto the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When a peg contains exactly a contiguous stack of the n smallest disks and the auxiliary peg is empty, and you need to relocate the whole stack to another peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempt moves the largest disk directly onto a smaller one without first moving the n‑1 smaller disks, causing a size‑ordering violation.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate move legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before committing a move, verify that the source peg’s top disk matches the disk you intend to move and that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: For every move you generate, perform this check before adding the move to the list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 from a peg where the top disk is 2, resulting in a non‑top move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use smallest disk as temporary buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without breaking the size rule, so use it to temporarily free pegs or to hold a spot while larger disks are moved.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to clear a peg but have no empty peg, move the smallest disk to the only available peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempt leaves a peg occupied by a larger disk, blocking the move of a needed larger disk, instead of moving the smallest disk to free it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat existing larger disks on target as base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already contains some of the final tower’s larger disks in the correct order, keep them untouched and build the remaining part of the tower on top.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the start of planning, identify any disks already correctly placed on the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 away from the goal peg even though it is already at the correct bottom position.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Iterative descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Assemble the final tower by handling disks from largest to smallest, placing each disk onto the goal peg after clearing any smaller disks from both its source and the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the final configuration, loop over disks in descending order and apply the clearing steps before each placement.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempt places disk 2 before disk 4, resulting in an incorrect final order.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the full sequence of moves, output it as the last syntactically correct list in the response, with no extra characters after the closing bracket.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the end of your answer, ensure the move list is the final thing printed.
tower-of-hanoi.example: The response ends with explanatory text after the move list, causing the parser to miss the list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear source and auxiliary pegs before moving a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the disk you want to move has any smaller disks on top of it (source peg) or the auxiliary peg you plan to use contains smaller disks, first relocate those smaller disks to another peg where they will not block the larger move, using the smallest disk as a buffer if needed.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that is not currently the top disk of its peg, or when you need an empty auxiliary peg for a recursive move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempt moves disk 4 from a peg where disk 3 is on top, resulting in a non‑top move error.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg before placing a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a larger disk onto its final peg, ensure that the target peg does not have any smaller disks on top; if it does, move those smaller disks to an auxiliary peg that is empty or has a larger top disk, again using the smallest disk as a temporary buffer if needed.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you are about to place a larger disk onto a peg that already contains disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempt moves disk 4 onto a peg where disk 2 is on top, violating the size rule.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model stops generation before emitting any moves, often due to focusing on reasoning text or hitting token limits.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always conclude with a syntactically correct move list, even if it is empty; ensure the move list is the final output.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (size ordering violation)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model forgets to check the destination peg's top disk before moving, especially when trying to place a disk quickly.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate move legality by comparing sizes of the moving disk and the destination top disk before adding the move.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk based on the goal position without confirming it's currently exposed.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the source peg's top disk matches the intended disk before moving.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model runs out of tokens or stops early, leaving the move list unfinished.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Plan a complete sequence before writing, and ensure the move list is fully printed before ending.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a disk from a peg where it is not present
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model mis‑tracks the state after several moves and assumes a disk is still on a peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain an explicit representation of the current configuration and update it after each move.
